fin_reserve.label: Build a cash reserve
case: A business that can't survive one bad week is a hobby with invoices. Keep enough back to cover the costs, and keep it there. The books say a week costs you {expenses}. The float stands at {float}, which is {weeks} weeks of that.

Costs arrive on schedule. Income, in my experience, does not. Hold back enough to meet the first without the second. Running costs: {expenses} a week. Float: {float}. The sum is {weeks} weeks. I did it twice, which is once more than you did.

You count your cash daily and your costs never. Count the costs. Then keep several weeks of them in the float. Your running costs come to {expenses} a week. Your float is {float}. Judge the gap yourself, or I will.

A float that covers weeks of costs, not days. Anything less is optimism, and I have seen what optimism invoices for. Cover today is {weeks} weeks of {expenses}. That is the number the bank will ask about, so you may as well know it first.

craft_first.label: Craft more {calc}
case: Selling the raw stuff is a start. Putting it into something is a business. Get our {calc} into more of what London crafts. The craft tally has you on {share}% of {calc}. {rival} is the name above yours.
Every bench in town burns {calc}. Make sure a fair slice of it is ours. {share}% of the {calc} crafted in London is ours. {rival} has the rest, and they aren't offering.

craft_rankup.label: Better work at the bench
case: Good enough sells once. Better sells twice. Take a recipe you already know and make it come out better than your best. Your best results are on the books. Beat them on any recipe you like. I'm not fussy which.
You've a bench full of competent. Push one recipe past your best result and see what the buyers do about it. Same recipes, same bench, higher mark. The bar is whatever you managed last time.

craft_master.label: Master a recipe
case: Rank five. Not near it, not nearly. A recipe done so well the bench looks embarrassed. You've got work at rank three or better on the books. The last two steps are the expensive ones.
Every trade has someone who's finished learning. Be that, for one recipe, and then for more. A recipe in the upper ranks already. Rank five is the same recipe, done properly.

share_first.label: A slice of {calc}
case: Take a quarter of London's {calc}. Then we're a name, not a rumour. James has been through the sheets. Contested ore at the moment: {contested}. {calc} is where you're strongest, at {share}%, and that's not nothing.

Right now nobody in the trade says our name without asking who we are. A quarter of the {calc} fixes that. James's tip, and he gave it me on a napkin: {contested} is where the factions are scrapping. You sit at {share}% of {calc}. Pick your lane.

We make the stuff. Buyers don't know it. Get a quarter of London's {calc} and they'll learn it quick. James says watch {contested}, because everyone else is. Your best ore is {calc} at {share}%. Start there or start nowhere.

A quarter of one ore. Doesn't have to be pretty, lads, just has to be ours. According to James, the contested ore is {contested}. You're on {share}% of {calc}, which is a foot in the door and no more.

share_higher.label: Push {calc} higher
case: A quarter was the start. Push {calc} higher and the factions notice. You're at {share}% of {calc}. The window still shows room, and {rival} is the one standing in it.
You've got your foot in. Now lean on the door. More {calc}, and we stop being polite about it. {share}% of {calc} this week. {rival} hasn't moved over for you yet.
Quarter's nice. Quarter gets you a nod in the pub. Half gets you a seat. The ticker has you on {share}% for {calc}. {rival} is the name next to yours.
Same ore, bigger bite. Don't look at me like that, you started it. {share}% and holding. {rival} sells the next biggest slice of {calc}, so that's who you're nicking it from.

share_leader.label: Lead the {calc} market
case: Not a share. The biggest share. Nobody sells more {calc} than us. You're at {share}% of {calc}, close enough to first place to smell it. {rival} is the one to beat.
Second place is just first place with a worse chair. Take the top spot on {calc}. {share}% on {calc} and {rival} is in the way. Nothing a few good weeks won't sort.
Own the lead, lads. When buyers say {calc}, they say our name first. The sheet gives you {share}% of {calc}. First place is {rival}'s chair until you sit in it.
Biggest seller of {calc} in London. I'd put it on the van, if we had a van. {share}%. That's a real number on {calc}. {rival} has noticed, so don't be shy.

share_leader_james.label: Lead the {calc} market
case: The Guild's standard for a leading house is the biggest share of one ore. Meet it on {calc}. You're at {share}% of {calc}, and {rival} is the name above yours.
A house that leads its ore is one the Guild has to deal with. Take first place on {calc}. {share}% today, with {rival} still ahead.

share_second.label: Second ore: {calc}
case: One ore is a niche. Take a slice of {calc} too. {calc} is on the sheet and you're at {share}%. Room to grow, and James says it won't wait.
All your eggs in one rock, that's how you end up in a pub talking about the good old days. Get into {calc}. You hold {share}% of {calc}. That's a start, and a second ore is what a start is for.
A second line of work. {calc} this time. Spread it out so one bad week doesn't take the lot. {share}% of {calc} today. Not much, but it's your second string and it's already in your hands.
You do one ore well. Do two and I'll start telling people you're a firm. You're on {share}% of {calc}, and it's moving. Get in while the number is small enough to double.

cult_yield.label: A bit more yield
case: If the veins gave a bit more than usual this week... only if that's all right. Your last ten days give a baseline, and a bit past it is the ask. Nothing heroic.
I've been watching the numbers. Not in a weird way. They could go up a little, I think. If we asked nicely. I averaged the last ten days. Twice. A bit above that is the whole plan.
Could we try for a bit past our usual? Just a bit. I've written the number down and then crossed it out. The ten-day average is the number to beat. Gently. Veins respond to gentle.

I had an idea about the yield. It's a small idea. I'll go first, so it's quicker if it's bad. Ten days of yield, averaged, is the line. I'd like us a little over it, and I'd like someone to tell me if that's daft.

cult_new_vein.label: Bring a vein online
case: There's a new vein that could come good. I could watch it. If you'd like. A fresh vein only counts once it's healthy enough to work. That's the bit I'd be watching.
There's one in the files nobody's looked at since you got it. I looked at it. It looked back, a bit. It has to get healthy first, then it counts. I'd check on it every morning, if that's allowed.
I'd like to try bringing a new vein up. I've read about it. I've read about it a lot. You've got a vein that isn't earning yet. Get it to working health and it's a new line on the sheet.
Archie says I should aim higher. This is higher. It's one vein higher. A vein that's only on paper doesn't count. A vein that's well enough to work does. I'd like the second kind.

cult_health_streak.label: Keep a vein healthy
case: A vein held in good condition night after night. Nobody's tried it properly. The nightly count only runs while a vein stays in good shape. One slip and it starts over.
I'd like to keep one vein well. Every night. I'll stay late, I don't mind. I've brought a flask. It's counted every night, and a bad night resets it. I know. I've thought about the bad night a lot.
It's not a big ask, it's a long one. A vein, kept in good shape, for days on the trot. A vein has to stay in good shape for the whole run of nights. The count doesn't forgive. I would.
What if one vein just... never had a bad night? I can't stop thinking about it. Each night it holds, the count goes up one. Each night it doesn't, it's back to nothing. I did warn you it was small.

cult_second_ore.label: A second ore
case: Not to alarm anyone, but we only have one kind of calc. Could we have two? Two ore types in good health means the business isn't one bad week from empty.
I keep thinking about the other kinds of calc. We don't have any. I keep thinking about that. If one ore has a bad week, the other doesn't. That's the whole argument. It's not a long one.
Could we grow a second sort of calc? I'll do the reading. I've already done the reading. A second ore, healthy enough to work, and the books stop leaning on one vein for everything.

James says one thing done well is a craft. Archie says one thing is a risk. Could I have a second thing? Both ores have to be in good shape for it to count. Two is steadier than one. I checked with the biscuits and it holds.

minutes._comment: Minutes reaction (BoardMeetings.minutes_line()). groups maps a history result to a reaction group; variant = entry week mod list size. Tokens: {label}, {tier}. skipped = the goal Archie picked for you (tuning.skipVoice). PROSE-REVIEW: all new copy.

full: Archie reads it off his phone. "{label}, {tier}. Don't make that face. It's a good number."
Archie holds the phone up like a receipt. "{label}, {tier}. Somebody frame that."
base: "{label}. Base." Archie nods slowly. "A pass. Barely. I'm putting 'barely' in the minutes."
"{label}, base only." Archie taps the screen. "Door's open and you walked through it. Politely."
missed: "{label}, missed." Archie pockets the phone. "Next week, then."
"{label} didn't land." He says it like a cancelled bus. "There's another one in seven days."

full: James leans over Archie's phone. "{label}, {tier}. Competent." He straightens. "Minute that word, Archie. Exactly that word."
James reads the line, then reads it again. "{label}, {tier}. Archie has spelled 'reached' with two e's. I have corrected it. The result stands."
base: James takes his glasses off to read it. "{label}, base. Technically a pass. The minutes will say so. My opinion I will record separately."
"{label}, base only." James frowns at the screen. "Archie wrote 'solid'. I'd have written 'adequate'. We will settle on 'base'."
missed: "{label}, missed." James folds his arms. "It was a reasonable number. Next week it can be a reasonable number again."
James squints at the phone. "'Not reached', Archie, not 'failed'. They are different words and I will defend the difference. {label}, not reached."

full: Owen leans in, finger under the line. "{label}, {tier}. That's good, yeah? That's the good one?"
Owen reads it twice to be sure. "{label}, {tier}. I'd like that noted. Not by me. By someone."
base: "{label}, base." Owen nods like it's a bonus. "That's a pass. Passes count. I'm counting it."
Owen reads the line. "Base on {label}. It's the one before the good ones. I'm choosing to see it as the start of the good ones."
missed: Owen winces on your behalf. "{label}, missed. It's one week. I missed a whole year of dentist."
Owen holds the phone like it's warm. "{label}, missed. Next week, then. I'll bring biscuits."

full: "{label}, {tier}." Archie reads it out with great calm. "My pick, that was. I'll take the credit. You weren't using it."
"I picked {label}. We hit {tier}." Archie puts the phone down. "I'm only saying it the once."
base: "{label}, base. Mine, so I'm calling it a solid pass." He looks at you. "You'd have said the same."
"I picked {label} and it made base." Archie considers this. "Next time pick your own and I'll complain about that instead."
missed: "Mine, {label}. Missed." Archie doesn't dress it up. "Next week, then. Pick something yourself."
"I picked {label} and it didn't land." He says it flat, no excuse. "Happens. Put the kettle on."

aob._comment: Any other business (BoardMeetings.aob_line()): one seeded line per meeting, never the same as last week's. competing = used instead when two offered cards want the same ore; tokens {a}, {b} (pitchers), {ore}. Running gags: James and the minutes, Archie's catering, Owen's unasked questions, Archie poaching Owen. PROSE-REVIEW: all new copy.
competing: Archie notes that {a} and {b} both want {ore}. Nobody offers to share.
James observes that {a} and {b} have pitched for the same {ore}. He asks that the minutes call it a coincidence.
Owen asks whether {a} and {b} know they want the same {ore}. They do. It's why the room is quiet.
Archie says {a} and {b} can fight over {ore} in the car park. Not today, he adds. The car park is booked.
lines: James asks that the minutes record the date correctly this time. Archie says he has. James says he has seen the minutes.
James would like it noted that 'any other business' is not a catch-all for Archie's opinions. Archie asks that his objection be noted.
James reads back the last item. It's a different item from the one Archie wrote down. They agree to keep James's.
James spots a typo in the minutes and asks who typed it. Archie says autocorrect. James says autocorrect has never once written 'calk'.
Archie raises catering. There is no budget for catering. Archie says that is the problem.
Archie proposes catering, in the sense of a Greggs run. James asks that it be minuted as 'refreshments'.
Archie says next week there will be catering. He says it the way people say they'll start running.
Archie asks if the biscuits count as catering. Owen says they were his. Archie says that settles it.
Owen raises a hand and asks who gets the last biscuit. Nobody knew there was a question.
Owen asks whether the whiteboard counts as a vein. Nobody has an answer ready.
Owen asks what happens to the minutes after the meeting. James says they are filed. Owen asks where. James does not say.
Owen asks if this is the meeting where they decide things or the one where they talk about deciding. Archie says yes.
Archie tells Owen his offer still stands: better money, a van, and a desk with a drawer that locks. Owen says he'll think about the drawer.
Archie mentions, to nobody, that Owen would be wasted on a bench. Owen looks at the bench.
Archie slides a business card across to Owen. James slides it back. Neither of them says a word about it.
Archie offers Owen a lift home. Owen says he has a bus. Archie says buses are a choice.
Nobody has any other business. James asks that this be minuted. Archie asks that it be minuted as a miracle.
James raises the kettle. It's his, he'd like it back, and he'd like to know who has been descaling it with lemon.
